title: Webb County Reports No Measles Cases as U.S., Mexico Lose Elimination Status
excerpt: Webb County has reported no measles cases even as the United States and Mexico lost their measles elimination status this month, and Laredo's public health director says the risk in the border city has not changed.
content:
Webb County has reported no measles cases, even as the United States and Mexico lost their measles elimination status this month after the virus circulated uninterrupted for more than a year, according to KGNS.

The Pan American Health Organization announced Nov. 17 that the United States, Mexico and Bolivia had lost the designation, after finding the same measles virus lineage had circulated continuously for 12 months or more in each country.

The United States eliminated measles in 2000 and held the status for 26 years. The current U.S. transmission chain traces back to Jan. 20, 2025, in West Texas, and Mexico's to Feb. 1, 2025.

Across the Americas, 58,213 confirmed measles cases and 82 deaths were recorded in 2026 through Nov. 13, according to the Pan American Health Organization. The United States has recorded 5,182 cases this year, and Mexico 13,796.

Laredo sits between the two countries, but Laredo Public Health Director Dr. Richard Chamberlain said the risk in the border city has not changed and the community remains protected, even though the virus has kept spreading across the country for more than a year, KGNS reported.

Health officials urge residents to check their vaccination status. Measles is highly contagious, and vaccination is the protection against it. Immunization services are offered at Laredo Public Health, 2600 Cedar Avenue.

Webb Watch 956 reported Nov. 14 that the United States had lost its elimination status. This report adds the local picture: no cases in Webb County.

Sources: KGNS — “Webb County reports no measles cases as U.S., Mexico lose elimination status”, Nov. 24, 2026; Pan American Health Organization, Nov. 17, 2026, https://www.theglobalvoice.com/us-mexico-and-bolivia-lose-measles-elimination-status-as-outbreaks-persist/
